what_it_does: Streaming high-quality virtual reality (VR) video from a server to a headset at the edge of a network is constrained by two competing demands: the wireless link is narrow, but VR requires smooth video at 90 frames per second to avoid motion sickness. Existing approaches sacrifice one or the other. Pirate exploits the fact that the two eye views in VR are nearly identical — a left-eye and right-eye frame of the same scene differ only by the small horizontal shift corresponding to eye separation. Instead of sending both, Pirate sends only one eye's view at a time, alternating between eyes across frames, together with precomputed geometric information (a depth map and motion field) that tells the headset exactly how to reconstruct the missing eye's view. The reconstruction runs as a lightweight geometric warp on the device — no large AI model needed — achieving claimed bitrates as low as 0.1 bits per pixel while maintaining 90 FPS.
